question: does Phase B's B0 arm inherit A0's budget, and why does it not reproduce A0 bit-for-bit?

measurements.pair: nested.fit_mlp_ensemble (local, macOS/Accelerate arm64) vs A0 shipped predictions
measurements.reading: bit-identical; A0 is reproducible from its own harness function

measurements.pair: phase_b.fit_arm_unit (local) vs nested.fit_mlp_ensemble (local), same platform and threads
measurements.reading: the loops are equivalent; residual is float32 summation order in the member mean, because fit_arm_unit round-trips predictions through Python lists to cross a Modal boundary

measurements.pair: phase_b.fit_arm_unit (local, macOS) vs phase_b.fit_arm_unit (Modal, Linux/OpenBLAS x86-64), both threads=1
measurements.reading: the whole discrepancy; cross-platform float32 accumulation order
identical magnitude to the row above, confirming the implementation term is negligible against the platform term

conclusion: The budget IS inherited: the implementation difference is 1.18e-06, five orders of magnitude below the platform term. Phase B's B0 differs from A0 because the batch ran on Linux/OpenBLAS x86-64 and A0 ran on macOS/Accelerate arm64, at matched threads=1. On the metric this is 0.0020 of median-of-medians (0.6473 against 0.6493). It does NOT affect any Phase B comparison: B0, B1 and B2 all ran in the same containers on the same platform at the same thread count, so every reported delta is against this study's own B0.
